newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee follows NY rally, ends off highs.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee follows NY rally, ends off highs.

text.p: Rallying New York coffee futures dragged London's robusta market higher on Friday but prices bumped into overhead resistance.
But trading was relatively slim due to extended Christmas holidays.
"It's moving but not making much headway. Before anyone can get excited about this market $1,280 must be broken. But every move up to $1,260 gets sold into," said one trader.
"London is constantly under pressure," he added.
Traders said the arabica market seemed to be boosted by fund buying as the CSCE March contract whisked past the 115 cent level. London was bid higher by industry and trade but activity was limited.

The key second-month March position saw a high of $1,260 a tonne -- an initial resistance area before $1,280 comes into play -- but quickly retreated to finish at $1,249, up $14 on the day. Others gained up to $29.
Turnover totalled 4,113 lots, including 1,000 lots of January AAs. The Jan/March switch traded from $35 to $38.
Market sources said earlier hedging by Vietnam had kept a lid on prices. March opened only $10 higher despite a call of some $30 up due to a strong New York finish on Tuesday.

Eyes are fixed on an upcoming independent assessment of the Brazilian coffee crop by former USDA analyst Leon Yallouz after a range of forecasts by trade houses and local sources resulted in conflicting views.
